extracted.intended_audience: researchers applying for Royal Society research funding (UK and overseas)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting applications to Royal Society research funding schemes, and explanation of how applications are assessed and decisions made. Covers eligibility, host-institution responsibilities, submission mechanics, assessment stages (panel, peer review, interview) and decision/feedback processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select the correct scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Find a scheme: Use filters to help focus your options and select the scheme that’s right for you. Open, close and decision dates for all schemes are available to view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look at what’s available and use filters; check open/close/decision dates; sign up for newsletters to receive latest information on Royal Society grants and opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check applicant eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that the research you are proposing to undertake falls within the natural sciences remit of the Royal Society. Shortly before each scheme opens, scheme pages are updated with any changes to eligibility criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the specific scheme pages for up-to-date eligibility for the round you intend to apply to; if unclear, contact the relevant team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check host organisation eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that your current/prospective host institution is eligible for the scheme by referring to the scheme notes. All UK HEIs that receive block funding and participate in REF and all Research Council Institutes are eligible. IROs and PSREs may be eligible if they meet criteria; private/commercial organisations in the UK may be eligible hosts for Industry Fellowships or Short Industry Fellowships only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Royal Society's position on eligible organisations for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read scheme notes in full
rubrics_metrics.description: Each scheme page contains scheme notes which give detailed information on the award, funding, references and application process. Some scheme pages will also have answers to Frequently Asked Questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheme notes contain scheme-specific eligibility, assessment stages and application details — read them fully and contact the relevant team for questions not addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss intention to apply with host department and research support
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss your intention to apply with your current or prospective host department and research support office as early as you can; they may be able to offer support and must be available to give consent before the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For fellowship applications discuss expected support if successful. For longer-term fellowships, discuss space, equipment/access requirements, additional resources (funding, students, technical support), proleptic appointments, professional development (mentor/training), and negotiate terms with the university where appropriate. Host organisation is not required to agree but many Research Fellows secure such support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight potential collaborations to research office
rubrics_metrics.description: Many programmes support and encourage collaboration (UK-UK, industry, or UK-overseas). Where collaborations are supported, these are usually funded through the UK host organisation; check scheme notes for specific collaboration eligibility and management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider legislative requirements (UK subsidy control regime, National Security and Investment Act) when collaborating, especially with industry or overseas organisations. Ensure appropriate frameworks for national security obligations and consult 'Trusted Research Guidance for Academia'. Have early discussions with your research office to navigate collaboration complexities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with Royal Society policy pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult policy pages for important information to consider before applying, including guidance on costing policy and expected standards for academic conduct. You will be required to comply with the policies, procedures and conditions of award if successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to grants policies and positions for further information and ensure your application aligns with these policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit via Flexi-Grant® and meet deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must be submitted through the grants management system, Flexi-Grant®. Applications received after the deadline will not be considered. Register and login; find Flexi-Grant overview and FAQs if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the system guidance and scheme notes for the submission process; contact grants@royalsociety.org for technical difficulties. Late submissions and missing host declarations mean applications will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain host organisation approval before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: For all single-stage applications and for stage 2 of two-stage applications the Research Office (or equivalent) must approve your application and carry out financial checks, and the Head of Department (or equivalent) must also give consent for you to hold your award within their department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some schemes require a statement of support from Head of Department and/or a nominated referee. It is the applicant’s responsibility to ensure all third-party statements of consent and support are submitted before the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial eligibility and completeness check
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications are checked for eligibility. The Grants Team will initially check all applications against the published eligibility criteria before they are submitted for panel assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application is found to be incomplete or ineligible it will be closed and the applicant notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel (Selection Committee) assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applications are assessed by a Selection Committee (Panel). Panels are chaired by a Fellow of the Royal Society and membership generally comprises scientists with expertise appropriate to each scheme. Each application is assessed by at least two Panel Members with the most relevant scientific expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following Panel assessments a shortlist is drawn up with oversight from the Panel Chair. Shortlisted applications may be recommended for funding or sent for independent peer review depending on scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment may include independent peer review and/or interview stages
rubrics_metrics.description: For some schemes the assessment process may include an independent peer review and/or interview stage. The assessment stages will be listed in the individual scheme notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check scheme notes to see if independent peer review or interview applies to your scheme and to learn the specific format and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary assessment criterion: scientific merit of individuals and proposed research
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applications are assessed against published criteria. Applications are primarily assessed based on scientific merit of the individual(s) and the research proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria for success are specific to each scheme and will be detailed in the individual scheme notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed equity, diversity and inclusion (EDI) principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The Royal Society regularly reviews policies and processes to embed EDI principles in all aspects of the grant-making process to ensure all applicants have an equitable chance to succeed as per assessment criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that EDI considerations form part of assessment design and implementation; consult scheme notes and policies for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent peer review scoring and confidential treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent peer reviewers (when used) are established researchers with expertise relevant to the application; they score and give constructive feedback on the application based on published assessment criteria and are instructed to treat applications with strictest confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers assess feasibility, novelty and significance of the proposed work and provide scored feedback which informs panel decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview assessment of candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: If the scheme has an interview stage, candidates invited will be provided with guidance on the purpose and format. Interviews usually take place at the Royal Society (may be online/hybrid) and you will be interviewed by members of the Panel; you may be asked to prepare a short presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After each interview, the quality of the candidate’s answers will be assessed by the Panel and used to inform funding recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final decision: scoring, ranking and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications reaching the final stage will be scored by the Panel and ranked using all available information (including independent peer review and interview score, if applicable). If more applications reach the required standard than available places, funding is awarded in rank order until places are allocated; some applications may be placed on a reserve list. The selection panel makes final recommendations which are approved by the Grants Committee before decisions are announced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision dates are scheme-specific; applicants are notified by email. Successful applicants receive an award letter detailing the offer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback to applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever possible, feedback is given to unsuccessful applicants. For most schemes, feedback from independent reviewers can be provided on request. Personalised feedback is not always possible, for example, in schemes with very high numbers of applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may request reviewer feedback where available; expect that personalised feedback may be limited in high-volume schemes.
